facts.statement: Padillasaurus was a titanosauriform sauropod that lived during the Early Cretaceous Barremian stage in Colombia.
facts.quote: Padillasaurus is an extinct genus of titanosauriform sauropod known from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian stage) Paja Formation in Colombia.

facts.statement: Local farmers discovered the fossil of Padillasaurus in a limestone nodule in Ricaurte, Colombia, during the 1990s.
facts.quote: The fossil was discovered by local farmers in a limestone nodule during the 1990s in Ricaurte, northeast of Villa de Leyva.

facts.statement: Padillasaurus was first described and named in 2015 by José L. Carballido and colleagues.
facts.quote: Padillasaurus was originally described and named by José L. Carballido, Diego Pol, Mary L. Parra Ruge, Santiago Padilla Bernal, María E. Páramo-Fonseca y Fernando Etayo-Serna in 2015.

facts.statement: The genus name Padillasaurus honors Carlos Bernardo Padilla, founder of the Centro de Investigaciones Paleontológicas in Villa de Leyva.
facts.quote: The name of the genus pays homage to Carlos Bernardo Padilla, the founder of the Centro de Investigaciones Paleontológicas in Villa de Leyva, Colombia.

facts.statement: The species name leivaensis refers to Villa de Leyva, near the discovery site of the holotype.
facts.quote: The specific name, leivaensis, is named after Villa de Leyva, which is located nearby to where the vertebrae of the holotype specimen were discovered.

facts.statement: The known fossils of Padillasaurus consist of torso, sacral, and tail vertebrae presumed to belong to a single individual.
facts.quote: The fossil consists of vertebrae from the torso, sacrum and tail: all presumed to be from one individual.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen JACVM 0001 includes a rear dorsal vertebra, the last two sacral vertebrae, and the first eight caudal vertebrae without chevrons.
facts.quote: This specimen is the holotype assigned to the catalogue number JACVM 0001; this includes a rear dorsal vertebra, a series from the last two sacral vertebrae and first eight caudal vertebrae (these caudal vertebrae were found without their chevrons).

facts.statement: Ammonite fossils in the rock matrix date the formation to the late Barremian, approximately 130 million years ago.
facts.quote: The rock matrix in which the fossil was located contains ammonite fossils bellowing to the species Gerhardtia galeatoides and Lytoceras sp., that allow the establishment of their origin in the middle Paja Formation which has been placed in the late Barremian, around 130 million years old.

facts.statement: Padillasaurus was a medium-sized titanosauriform dinosaur.
facts.quote: Padillasaurus was a medium-sized titanosauriform.

facts.statement: Based on limited remains, Padillasaurus may have reached 16 to 18 meters in length and weighed about 10 tonnes.
facts.quote: Because of the few remains found it is difficult to determine what would have been its body size, but it may have been between 16 - 18 m long and weighed about 10 t.

facts.statement: Padillasaurus is distinguished by its caudal vertebrae being weakly expanded to the sides with divided side projections.
facts.quote: Padillasaurus is distinguished from other titanosauriforms in having its caudal vertebrae weakly expanded to the sides, and displaying divided side projections.

facts.statement: The vertebrae of Padillasaurus are opisthocoelic, featuring a convex front and concave back.
facts.quote: The vertebra is opisthocoelic, with a convex front section and the back concave.

facts.statement: The vertebrae of Padillasaurus possess large pleurocoels, pneumatic processes connecting to hollow cavities within the bone.
facts.quote: The edges show large pleurocoels, pneumatic processes that connected to the hollow interior of the body of the vertebra, which consisted of several hollow cavities.

facts.statement: An additional lamina was present on the spine between the diapophysis and the vertebral body.
facts.quote: The spine also had an additional lamina between the diapophysis and the body of the vertebra.

facts.statement: The neural arches are positioned relatively forward and feature long ridges running between joint face protuberances and the vertebral body.
facts.quote: The neural arches are positioned relatively forward. These have long ridges that run between the protuberances of the joint face and body of the vertebra.

facts.statement: The side projections on the vertebrae are oriented obliquely backward and have a convex lower area.
facts.quote: The side projections are oriented obliquely backwards and have a convex lower area.

facts.statement: The caudal vertebrae of Padillasaurus have a height equal to half their width.
facts.quote: The caudal vertebrae have a height equal to half of its width.

facts.statement: Padillasaurus was initially classified as a brachiosaurid and considered the first named South American brachiosaurid.
facts.quote: Initially described as a brachiosaurid, it was considered to be the first South American brachiosaurid ever discovered and named.

facts.statement: A more recent study reclassified Padillasaurus as a basal member of the Somphospondyli.
facts.quote: However, a more recent study finds it to be a basal somphospondylan.

facts.statement: Padillasaurus was initially placed in the family Brachiosauridae based on its morphology.
facts.quote: Padillasaurus was initially classified in the family Brachiosauridae based on its morphology.

facts.statement: Cavities in the sacral vertebrae lacking connection to the hollow interior, a lack of true pleurocoel, linked Padillasaurus to brachiosaurids.
facts.quote: It had cavities in the sacral vertebrae that had no connection with the hollow interior of the vertebra, therefore lacking a true pleurocoel. This feature links it to the brachiosaurids.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis found Padillasaurus in a polytomy with other basal forms like Abydosaurus, Brachiosaurus, and Giraffatitan, with Cedarosaurus and Venenosaurus occasionally as sister taxa.
facts.quote: A cladistic analysis was unable to determine the exact relationships of Padillasaurus with other genera, finding a polytomy among basal forms including Padillasaurus, Abydosaurus, Brachiosaurus and Giraffatitan, while Cedarosaurus and Venenosaurus were occasionally recovered as sister taxa.

facts.statement: Unlike North American Cretaceous brachiosaurids, the spinous processes of Padillasaurus's caudal vertebrae angled rearward.
facts.quote: Unlike Cretaceous brachiosaurids from North America, in which the spinous process of the caudal vertebrae leaned slightly forward, those of Padillasaurus were angled rearward.

facts.statement: Padillasaurus is classified within the unranked family Somphospondyli.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Somphospondyli

facts.statement: Padillasaurus represents the first record of a Cretaceous brachiosaurid from South America, whereas previous Cretaceous brachiosaurid findings were only known from North America.
facts.quote: Padillasaurus is the first record of a Cretaceous brachiosaurid of South America; previous findings of that time were only known in North America.

facts.statement: Padillasaurus is the latest known brachiosaurid from the ancient continent of Gondwana.
facts.quote: It is also the latest brachiosaurid known from the ancient continent of Gondwana.

facts.statement: Padillasaurus was originally classified in the family Brachiosauridae based on its morphology.
facts.quote: Padillasaurus fue situado originalmente en la familia Brachiosauridae basándose en su morfología.

facts.statement: The dinosaur has cavities in the sacral vertebrae that do not connect to the hollow interior of the vertebra, meaning it lacks a true pleurocoel.
facts.quote: Este dinosaurio tiene cavidades en las vértebras sacrales que no tienen conexión con el interior hueco de la vértebra, y por tanto carece de un verdadero pleurocelo.

facts.statement: This trait relates it to the brachiosaurids.
facts.quote: Este rasgo lo relaciona con los braquiosáuridos.

facts.statement: A cladistic analysis could not determine exact relationships, placing Padillasaurus in a basal polytomy with Abydosaurus, Brachiosaurus, Giraffatitan, Cedarosaurus, and Venenosaurus, which sometimes became sister taxa.
facts.quote: Un análisis cladístico fue incapaz de determinar las relaciones exactas de Padillasaurus con otros géneros, por lo cual termina en una politomía de formas basales en la que se incluyen a Padillasaurus, Abydosaurus, Brachiosaurus y Giraffatitan junto con Cedarosaurus y Venenosaurus, que ocasionalmente terminaron siendo taxones hermanos.

facts.statement: It lacks a typical Cretaceous North American brachiosaurid trait: the anterior caudal vertebral spinous process angles backward instead of slightly forward.
facts.quote: Padillasaurus carece de una característica típica de los braquiosáuridos de Norteamérica del Cretácico, que es el proceso espinoso de las vértebras anteriores caudales que se inclina levemente hacia adelante; en cambio, este tiene un ángulo dirigido hacia atrás.

facts.statement: It is the first record of a Cretaceous brachiosaurid from South America, as previous findings from that period were known only from North America.
facts.quote: Es el primer registro de un braquiosáurido del Cretácico de América del Sur; hallazgos previos de ese periodo solo se conocían en Norteamérica.

facts.statement: It is also the most recent known brachiosaurid from the ancient continent of Gondwana.
facts.quote: Asimismo, es el braquiosáurido más reciente conocido del antiguo continente de Gondwana.

facts.statement: However, a 2017 study concluded that Padillasaurus was not a brachiosaurid but a basal member of the group Somphospondyli.
facts.quote: No obstante, un estudio publicado en 2017 llegó a la conclusión de que Padillasaurus no era un braquiosáurido, sino un miembro basal del grupo Somphospondyli.

facts.statement: Its parent group is Somphospondyli.
facts.quote: Parent group: Somphospondyli

facts.statement: It belongs to the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: It lived during the Barremian stage, from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)
